subject: biology
title: Cell Biology Adventure 3: Mitosis and the cell cycle
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the cell cycle — interphase, mitosis, cytokinesis — and the cyclins that drive it.
meta_desc: Biology — cell cycle phases, mitosis stages, cyclins, mutation and cancer.
final_note: You learned the cell cycle is G1→S→G2→M, mitosis has PMAT stages, cyclins activate CDKs, and uncontrolled division causes tumours.

concepts.def: G1 + S + G2; cell grows and replicates DNA
Nuclear division yielding two identical nuclei
Regulatory protein activating CDKs at checkpoints

walkthroughs.body_html:
The cell cycle has four phases:

- G1 — growth, organelles replicate.
- S — DNA replication, 2n → 4n DNA.
- G2 — final growth, error checking.
- M — mitosis + cytokinesis.

Cyclins bind CDKs (cyclin-dependent kinases) to phosphorylate targets and push through checkpoints (Nurse + Hunt, Nobel 2001).

Prophase — chromosomes condense, nuclear envelope breaks, spindle forms.
Metaphase — chromosomes align at equator.
Anaphase — sister chromatids pulled to poles.
Telophase — nuclei reform, chromosomes decondense.

Then cytokinesis — animal cells pinch (cleavage furrow), plant cells build a cell plate.

Mutations in proto-oncogenes (gain of function) or tumour suppressor genes like p53 cause uncontrolled mitosis.

Carcinogens include UV, tobacco tar and certain viruses (HPV → cervical cancer). Globally, ~10 million cancer deaths/year (WHO, 2020).

Mitotic index = (cells in mitosis) / (total cells) — higher in tumours.
